title: Drafting Proposal Responses
answer: Drafting proposal responses in finance covers the use of AI agents to assemble answers to requests for proposals, due diligence questionnaires, and client pitch documents. It spans investment management, banking, insurance, and corporate finance. The work includes pulling boilerplate, tailoring content to the prospect, checking compliance language, and producing a first draft for a human to review. It is not autonomous deal-making; the agent supports the proposal team.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Drafting proposal responses in finance covers the use of AI agents to assemble answers to requests for proposals, due diligence questionnaires, and client pitch documents. It spans investment management, banking, insurance, and corporate finance. The work includes pulling boilerplate, tailoring content to the prospect, checking compliance language, and producing a first draft for a human to review. It is not autonomous deal-making; the agent supports the proposal team.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: This typically runs on secure document repositories, CRM systems, and internal knowledge bases connected to a large language model. The model may be hosted in a private cloud or on premises because proposal content includes confidential fee structures, performance data, and client names. Access is usually role-based, and the agent logs every query and source document it retrieves.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The agent retrieves past winning proposals, standard disclosures, and product fact sheets, then fills a template with the prospect's name, dates, and specific questions. It scores each answer against the question to catch off-topic text and flags missing data for a human. A subject matter expert reviews the draft, edits the tone, and approves the final version before it goes out.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Every sentence in a draft should trace back to an approved source document, and the system keeps that mapping for audit. The main risks are hallucinated performance figures, stale fee schedules, and reuse of another client's confidential terms. Compliance teams set rules about which sources the agent may cite and which claims require a human sign-off. Ownership of the draft remains with the firm, but third-party model providers may see prompts unless the deployment is fully private.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Proposal drafting is moving from single-shot text generation to multi-agent workflows where one agent checks the question, another drafts, and a third verifies numbers against a data room. Firms are starting to connect these agents to live CRM and portfolio data so drafts reflect the latest figures without manual copying. The likely next step is a negotiation-aware assistant that tracks what was promised in the proposal and flags conflicts when the contract is drafted. Human review will remain the final gate for anything sent to a client.
